seen.extent: One letter of two pages (Asunción, 13 Feb 1850, signed Benito Varela, to the Consul General in Rio): 12 runs of dot-separated numbers, about 90 cipher tokens, plus single numbers standing for persons (25 twice, 1 twice, 116) and one barred-circle sign; the rest of the letter is clear Spanish.
seen.cipher: Numeric substitution, almost all values odd and below 50 (plus 98 and 116), in runs of 2-16 numbers embedded in clear text: a letter table with homophones or a small syllabary, plus a few name numbers. No decipherment, interlining or key is written on or with the letter (images 38-45 checked).

prior_art.edition: No edition of the Varela - Moreira de Castro correspondence was found: web searches for the correspondents with 'correspondencia cifrada' returned only the ANA AtoM catalogue records (Moreira de Castro letters of 1853, Varela's appointment); the ANA description of item 13 itself says the passages could not be identified because they are 'escritos en código cifrado'. Printed Paraguayan diplomatic collections were not checked page by page.
prior_art.literature: Web searches in Spanish and English on Carlos Antonio López's diplomatic ciphers (cifra diplomática Paraguay, clave cifrada siglo XIX, criptografía) found no study of a Paraguayan state cipher of this period.

vetting.key_check: No Paraguayan key of the López era is held in the repo or known in print. The sibling diplomatic files of the Rio Branco collection skimmed in the South Cone sweep (Gelly in Rio 1849-52, Decoud 1853, F. S. López 1853, Varela - Derqui 1852) showed no number runs at thumbnail size, and the other 96 images of this file were not paged through for a key in this session. Quick checks here: the repeated runs (9.27.7.33.15.3 twice; 9.13.1.37.3.1?.7.9.33 twice before '[Rio?] Grande') do not fit a plain one-value-per-letter alphabet with an obvious crib ('provincia' would need two values for i and one value for both r and n), so no simple key tried reads it. Not a key lookup on present evidence.
